packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-02 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (blind first reader)

EXPOSURE / PROCEDURE STATEMENT
- No proposed identification of the work or author reached me before or during this reading.
- The images carry modern pencil shelf marks ("Stams, STA, Frg. 39-1v", "-2v", "-5r", "-5v", "-6r", "-6v", "-7r", "-7v", "-8r", "-8v", "STA 39-9r", "STA 39-9v") and a pencil binding note "aus Einband II/6 ab (ca. 1534)". These are archive labels, not text identifications. I report them because they are visible.
- I did nothing beyond the brief: I opened only PROMPT.md and image files in this packet directory, used no search or web tool and did not read packet.json.
- TECHNICAL LIMITATION: images 001-013, 015, 016, 018 and 019 did not load. The viewer returned "media removed: request limit" for them, so I have NOT seen them. Image 014 and image 017 loaded. They show blank paper faces (pencil labels "39-2v" and "39-1v") with stains, sewing slits, a hole and a pencil sketch, but no visible script. So the faces covered by images 001-019 (apparently Frg. 39 leaves 1-2) are UNREAD except for those two blank tiles. Please re-run those images.
- Images 020-040 loaded and are the basis of everything below.

LAYOUT SURVEY (images 020-040; observations)
- Image 020 is an overview of one side and image 031 of the other. Each shows five paper pieces on black: two bifolium-sized pieces (labelled 5 and 6), one oblong sheet folded down the middle (7), a small rectangle (8) and a tiny strip (9). Colour chart and ruler.
- The paper is unruled and has no rubrics, running titles or decorated initials. It is written in 16th-century-looking German cursive (Kurrent) mixed with Latin, in several hands and inks.
- 5r, 5v (left half) and 6r (right half): a NUMBERED LIST (1., 2., 3. ... 9.) in the margin. Each number has a pair of lines joined by curly brackets: a Latin sentence, then a German sentence. This looks like a school exercise of Latin proverbs or phrases with German renderings (tentative interpretation).
- 5v (right half), 6r (left half) and 6v: blocks of Latin and German lines, some bolder in a darker ink. They look like vocabulary or phrase pairs.
- 7r/7v: drafts of German letter openings ("Mein sonndern freundtlich ...") mixed with pen trials: alphabet rows "a a a a ...", "aabcdefghiklmnopq ...", and isolated letters. Some lines are struck through.
- 8r: small piece with 5 lines of German cursive. 8v: no clear script (stains, a faint drawn curve).
- 9r/9v: tiny strip with ink traces, illegible.
- The left edge of 6r's left column and the right edges of 5v and 7r are cropped by the paper edge or by plastic weights. Bottom lines of 5r are under a clear weight.

CONVENTIONS: (x) = proposed expansion; x? = uncertain reading; [illegible]; "{" = bracket in MS. Line numbers count from the top of the named image. Overlapping tiles are noted and not double-counted.
